summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with IgA multiple myeloma on carfilzomib, was admitted for worsening cellulitis around a chronic left leg ulcer after using a hot tub. He was afebrile and denied pain. Blood cultures were negative, but wound cultures grew group B strep, Bacteroides fragilis, and coagulase-negative staph. He was treated with IV antibiotics, initially cefepime then switched to piperacillin-tazobactam (Zosyn) for a 14-day course to be completed at home via a newly placed PICC line. MRI and X-ray ruled out osteomyelitis. His chemotherapy was held during admission and successfully resumed prior to discharge. He also received IV furosemide for acute on chronic diastolic heart failure, with improvement in edema, and was restarted on oral lasix. His hemolytic anemia remained stable on prednisone, and diabetes was managed with insulin. He was discharged home in stable condition with plans for follow-up in oncology, infectious disease, and primary care.
